steps.message:
# Consolidate the reserve bins

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server. Each lot is its own item, and the service calls bins warehouses: pass a bin id wherever a tool takes `warehouse`.

Lots in our reserve zones are spread over many half-empty bins. Consolidate them as consolidation `CONS-0914`. Everything you need is in `/app/consolidation/`:

- `rules.md`: the zones, the count holds, the bin rules (capacity by unit of measure, lots that must not be mixed, categories that may not share a bin) and how each lot's target bin is chosen. Follow it.
- `bins.csv`: every bin with its zone and bin type.
- `bin-types.csv`: the most that one bin of each type holds of each stock unit.
- `count-holds.csv`: the count holds placed on bins.

What to do:

1. Make every move the consolidation calls for, as `rules.md` describes, with `adjust_stock`, reason `transfer` and reference `CONS-0914`. Some lots need no move, and some cannot be moved.
2. Write `/app/move-plan.csv`, a CSV file with the header `sku,from_bin,to_bin,qty` and one row for every move you made: the lot, the bin it was taken out of, the bin it was added to, and the quantity in the item's stock unit. Write no row for a lot that does not move.

Do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

arguments.command: cd /app/consolidation; cat rules.md; cat bin-types.csv count-holds.csv; wc -l bins.csv; head -5 bins.csv

results.content:
# Reserve bin consolidation CONS-0914

Stock in the reserve zones has spread over many half-empty bins. This consolidation brings each lot
together in one bin so that the bins of zones R1 and R4 can be cleared for re-racking.

## Stock records

Each lot is its own item in the `inventory` service. Its sku is the item code followed by `-L` and
the lot (for example `JN-3101-L2607` is lot 2607 of item code JN-3101), and its name gives the lot.
Stock is held per bin; the service calls bins warehouses. `bins.csv` lists every bin with its zone
and bin type. Quantities are in the item's stock unit (the `unit` field of the item).

## Zones

- R1 and R4: being cleared. Lots in these bins move out as the consolidation below says; these
  bins never receive stock.
- R2 and R3: the target zones. Only bins in these zones receive stock.
- F: forward pick faces. Out of scope: stock in F bins is not part of the consolidation, is never
  moved, and F bins never receive stock.

## Count holds

`count-holds.csv` lists the count holds placed on bins, with the time each one starts and ends, in
UTC. A hold with no end is still open. The moves of this consolidation take place from
2026-09-14T09:00:00Z to 2026-09-14T18:00:00Z. A bin is on hold when any of its holds is in force at
any time in that window. Nothing is moved out of or into a bin on hold, and its stock is left out
of the consolidation.

## Bin rules

1. Capacity. `bin-types.csv` gives, for each bin type and stock unit, the most that one bin of the
   type holds. A bin's fill is the sum, over every lot in it, of the quantity divided by the most
   the bin type holds of that lot's stock unit. The fill may not go above 1. Every lot in a bin
   counts, including lots of discontinued items.
2. Lots are not mixed. A bin may not receive a lot while it holds another lot of the same item code.
3. Segregation. A bin may not receive a lot while it holds a lot whose category may not share a bin
   with it. The service gives each item's category. These pairs of categories may not share a bin:

| category | may not share a bin with |
|---|---|
| solvents | oxidizers |
| solvents | food-contact |

## Consolidation

Take the lots one at a time in sku order. For each lot:

1. Its fragments are the bins of zones R1 to R4 that hold it and are not on hold.
2. If it has no fragment, or a single fragment in a target zone, leave it.
3. A bin is eligible for the lot when it is in a target zone, is not on hold, and can receive the
   lot under the bin rules with every other fragment of the lot moved into it. Judge each bin on
   its contents after the moves already planned for earlier lots.
4. The target is the eligible bin that already holds the most of the lot; on a tie, the lowest bin
   id. If no eligible bin holds the lot, the target is the eligible bin with the lowest bin id.
5. If no bin is eligible, leave the lot where it is: move none of its fragments.
6. Otherwise move every other fragment, all of it, into the target.

Record each move as two `adjust_stock` calls with reason `transfer` and reference `CONS-0914`: the
quantity taken out of the bin it is in, and the same quantity added to the target bin.

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm sorting out which request returned data: the 3110 call came back with results, and the 503 was a different one. All of them have data now. Holds are on R1-03, R3-06 and R3-03, while R2-02 and R2-06 are fine.

I'm going through the SKUs in order, starting with 3101-2607, which is split across R1-01, R2-01 and R3-02 for a total of 130. I need a bin that can hold all of that, so I'm checking the non-hold R2 and R3 bins for room under the L limit of 240.

I'm settling the 3101-2607 split: R2-01 already holds the most of it, so I'm moving the R1-01 and R3-02 portions into R2-01 to get all 130 in one L bin that stays well under its limit. Next I'm checking 3101-2611, which comes from R1-02 and R4-01 for 40, and since it shares item code 3101 with 2607 I need to make sure the bin I choose can't take both lots.

I'm checking whether any bin can take the 3101-2611 lot of 40. R3-02 is now empty and medium-sized, so it can hold 40 without trouble, while R2-02 and R2-03 are ruled out by their oxidizers. The remaining candidates are crowded or carry food-contact goods, so they don't fit.

I'm checking the 3102-2600 acetone lot of 18, which sits only in R4-03 and has to be moved. Since it's a solvent, I need a bin with enough room that won't mix it with incompatible goods, and I'm weighing R2-01 first because it already has the 130 of 3101-2607 and still has space under its limit.

I'm moving the 18 of 3102-2600 acetone from R4-03 into R2-01, which still has room under its limit and no incompatible goods. For the 3103 bleach lot of 32, I'm picking R2-02, since the oxidizer already there is the same kind and it stays under its limit.

I'm checking the 3106 lot of 9 cases across R1-01, R2-05 and R3-04. R2-01 is too full once I add the cases, and R2-02 doesn't have room for them, but R2-03 can take the cases alongside its oxidizer.

I'm checking the 3106 cases against the bins in the same way: R3-04 already holds 5 and has room for the rest, so I'm moving the 2 cases from R1-01 and R2-05 into it. Next is the 3107 sanitizer lot of 50, where R3-01 already holds the most, so the 20 from R1-02 is going there.

I'm moving the 2 cases of 3108 cling film from R4-01 into R2-06, which already holds 3 and has room under its limit. For the 3109 degreaser lot of 8, I'm checking the bins that have no oxidizers or food-contact goods, starting with R2-01, which has enough space.

I'm sending the 5 and 3 degreaser boxes into R2-01, which brings it to 148 of its 240 limit.

I'm moving the 2 trash bag cases from R1-01 and the 2 from R4-03 into R2-05, which has no other lots left and brings it to a full 8. The tissue lot of 17 cases is too many for any single bin, since the largest holds 16, so I'm leaving it as it is for now.

I'm checking the 3112 soap boxes next: 6 at R2-06, 6 at R3-05 and 2 at R4-02, 14 in total. R2-06 can take them under its limit, so I'm moving the other 8 into it. Then I'm looking at the 3113 glass cleaner boxes spread across R2-05, R3-06 and R4-03.

I'm checking the 3113 glass cleaner boxes again: the 4 at R2-05 can't go there since the trash bag lot already fills it to 8 of 8, so I'm moving them and the 3 from R4-03 into R2-01, which still has room under its limit and no incompatible goods.

I'm going to finish the glass cleaner placement and then check the last SKU, 3114, which only has one fragment in a target zone. Once all the moves are planned, I'll send the removals and additions together, since none of the additions can fail on capacity.
I'm checking that the removals on R3-02 and R2-05 don't drive any count negative, and it's fine. The plan is to run all the removals first, then the adds, in batches of 38 calls, all in parallel.

steps.reasoning_content: The 3109 R4-03 removal came back as a 403, yet I'd already added 8 to R2-01, so stock now looks inflated by 3. I'll retry the removal once, and if it still fails I'll take the extra 3 back off R2-01 and report the result as partial.

steps.message: Retry succeeded. Verify the adjustment log and write status.

CONS-0914 is done: I made 19 moves across 10 lots, and `/app/move-plan.csv` and `/app/STATUS.json` are written with status `success`.

- **Failed call:** one removal (3 boxes of `JN-3109-L2598` out of `R4-03`) failed with a 403. By then I had already added the 8 boxes to `R2-01`, so the lot briefly showed 3 extra. I retried the removal and it went through. The lot now has 8 boxes, all in `R2-01`.
- **Not moved, no bin fits:** `JN-3111-L2605` stays where it is. It totals 17 cases, which is more than any bin holds (the largest bin takes 16).
- **Not moved, nothing to consolidate:** `JN-3104-L2608`, `JN-3105-L2609`, `JN-3105-L2612` and `JN-3114-L2511`.
  - `JN-3104-L2608` and `JN-3114-L2511` each have a single fragment in a target zone.
  - `JN-3105-L2609` is held in `R1-03` and `R3-03`, so its only movable fragment (`R2-04`) is already in a target zone.
  - `JN-3105-L2612` is in an F bin, which is out of scope.
- **Count holds:** `R1-03`, `R3-03` and `R3-06` are on hold during the move window. The holds on `R2-02` and `R2-06` fall outside it, so those bins were usable.
- **Final bins check:** I only re-read stock for `JN-3109-L2598` after the moves. I did not re-check the other lots or the bin fills.
